findings.claim: In salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, getClient bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so the credential sync endpoint is never called in sync mode.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-84 calls fetch on https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token directly and never imports or calls refreshOAuthTokens (only parseRefreshTokenResponse is imported, line 20). The CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT branch in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-15 is therefore never reached for Salesforce, unlike hubspot, zoho, zoom and the other apps that wrap their refresh in it.

findings.claim: In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, refreshOAuthTokens is passed credentialId (credential.id) as its third argument, which is userId. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong calcomUserId.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:53 sets credentialId = credential.id and line 93 passes it as the third argument of refreshOAuthTokens, whose third parameter is userId and is sent as calcomUserId (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3,11). When credential sharing is enabled, the sync endpoint is therefore given the credential's id instead of the user's id.

findings.claim: minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()]. These evaluate to literal, colliding property names instead of dynamic key matchers, so real token payloads fail validation or have every field except access_token stripped.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 and :10 use `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as computed keys; Zod v3 schemas do not override `toString`, so both become the literal key "[object Object]" and the second overwrites the first. The schema is effectively `{access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown}`, so in the credential-sync branch (line 16) payloads still validate but default `z.object` stripping drops expiry and every other field (the 'fail validation' alternative does not occur). Not executed; zod is not installed in this checkout.

findings.claim: In sync mode, Salesforce getClient parses the response with the stripping minimum schema, which drops instance_url and other fields.

findings.claim: In the credential webhook handler, appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body), symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse run without error handling. Malformed bodies, bad ciphertext, a wrong key or invalid JSON therefore return 500 instead of 4xx.

findings.claim: The webhook header lookup does not handle array values. A header sent multiple times yields an array, and the string comparison against it lets the request through.

findings.claim: Office365 loses its expiry fields in sync mode, so a token refresh happens on every call.

findings.claim: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts persists stale credentials when token parsing fails instead of throwing an error.

findings.claim: The webhook's read-then-write credential upsert can create duplicate credentials under concurrent requests because there is no unique constraint.

verifier.reason: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-92 does a `findFirst` on (userId, appId) followed by a separate `create` with no transaction or lock, and the `Credential` model in packages/prisma/schema.prisma:127-146 has only non-unique `@@index([userId])` and `@@index([appId])`, so two concurrent requests can both miss the lookup and each insert a row.

findings.claim: In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, appConfig.slug was replaced with the literal 'zoho-bigin', while appConfig.slug is still used on line 12.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts never imports or uses appConfig (line 12 is a type import of NewCalendarEventType), and the patch only adds a new "zoho-bigin" literal argument at line 92 rather than replacing anything. findings.claim: The decrypted keys are written to credential.key without shape validation.

verifier.reason: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59 assigns `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` to `keys`, which is written straight to `credential.key` at lines 78 and 85 with no zod or per-app schema check; the request schema at lines 9-15 only requires `keys` to be a string. The caller must already hold the webhook secret and the encryption key, so the exposure is limited to a trusted sender storing malformed credentials.

findings.claim: The external fetch in refreshOAuthTokens has no timeout.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 calls fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method, body }) with no signal/AbortController or other timeout, and nothing in packages/app-store/_utils adds one; only the runtime's default fetch limits would apply, which I did not check here.
